observations: Despite running inside a coding-agent harness, the model completed the challenge in a single zero-tool turn and returned raw HTML without markdown fences or prose.

The 1,630-line (58,361-byte) response uses a 3-layer hybrid architecture: a background 2D canvas for parallax scenery, an articulated inline SVG rig for the capybara and hoverboard, and a foreground 2D canvas for particle effects.
Both canvases replicate the SVG 1200x750 viewBox aspect-ratio transform on resize so exhaust particles and repulsor rings stay aligned with the vector hoverboard.

Animation includes harmonic hover oscillation, velocity-coupled board pitch, spring-damper physics on a stackable yuzu, dynamic scarf path morphing, autonomous trick timers, and keyboard, pointer, and button controls across three color themes.
The response is self-contained with no external assets, libraries, fonts, network calls, or audio, and uses Math.random for scenery, particles, and autonomous trick timing.

Recorded usage totals 37,171 tokens (8,952 input, 0 cached, and 28,219 output including 5,200 thinking tokens); model time is null because the session records thinking duration and step timestamps rather than assistant durationMs.
